setup: Grasp an overhead pull-up bar with an overhand grip roughly shoulder-width apart.
Step or lower off the platform into a full hang with straight arms and feet off the floor.
steps: Actively pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears without bending your elbows.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes lightly to maintain a stable, hollow body position.
Hold this active shoulder-depressed position for the target duration.
Carefully lower your shoulder blades into a relaxed hang or step down to conclude the set.
instructions.breathing: Maintain steady, rhythmic breathing through your diaphragm while keeping your core braced and shoulders packed.
cues: Stay long and hollow through your torso

common_faults.fault: Bending the elbows to pull the body upward.
common_faults.correction: Keep your arms completely straight; the movement should come entirely from scapular depression.

common_faults.fault: Allowing shoulders to shrug up to the ears (collapsing into a passive dead hang).
common_faults.correction: Continuously engage your lats and mid-back to keep space between your shoulders and ears.

common_faults.fault: Excessive arching of the lower back.
common_faults.correction: Engage your abs and point your toes slightly forward to keep a neutral spine.

precautions: Ensure the bar is secure and can support your full body weight.
Step down safely rather than dropping from excessive heights if grip fatigue sets in.

name: Active Hang
summary: An isometric bodyweight hold from an overhead bar with shoulders actively depressed and stabilized.
